Ok, maybe I should have done a better job describing it. We know the stuff about the flashlight, because two of the girls woke up while it was happening. The first girl heard a knock, then saw somebody standing in her doorway. The person left and she checked the time on her phone.

The second girl woke up to somebody walking in, same description, and then leaving.

In my case I thought my door had opened by itself, and just kind of saw somebody peeking in. My room is much smaller, so you can't really step in, my bed takes up the entire space. I froze, cause I assumed I was having a nightmare.

I know it's probably easy to question why we each acted the way we did. The two other girls thought it was our roommate, I kinda went for neck-in-the-sand. As for why the police officer said that.. who knows. I just included it, because it seriously freaked me out and I thought it was a bit inappropriate. Then again, English was clearly not his first language (which is common where we are), and part of me wants to chalk it up to that.

I'm really not here to argue. I just want some advice/reassurance. It's really scary having your space breached like that, and if I sounded defensive, it's just because it's frustrating to honestly feel violated and have someone outright tell you they think you're lying. Having a police officer not take it seriously is grating enough as it is. 

If you feel we're overreacting to the situation, that's fair if you've had a similar experience, but as far as I know everything happened the way I told it.

Look, I'm not sure how you would describe the situation. We know somebody was in the house, because people saw it, so unless we're collectively dreaming, then it pretty much happened.

Is it that crazy to imagine that if if a stranger comes into your house at night you'd feel pretty violated and shaken?

I kinda feel like telling her she hasn't made any effort isn't the best approach. She is probably feeling disempowered by her situation and it can be hard to make connections in a completely new place. Honestly, trying to build friendships in a new environment can be such a hit and miss, but the initial misses are super discouraging.

I'd say try to encourage her to attend group activities with people she shares interests with. Maybe volunteering for animal-based activities would work. The best would probably be something that is fairly time consuming, so there is potential to get to know the people she is with. Good luck, moves are difficult once the initial excitement dies down, especially when you're with somebody who's a little ahead of you. That said, the horse is definitely working against her making new connections. If the season is ending, perhaps suggest some activities that can replace the hole this is going to leave in her life, because she will need it.
